facts: ZF Friedrichshafen AG was founded in 1915 by Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin and Alfred von Soden-Fraunhofen.
The company is headquartered in Friedrichshafen, Baden-Württemberg, Germany.
As of 2025, ZF Friedrichshafen AG employs approximately 153,000 people.
ZF is a global technology company supplying advanced mobility products and systems for passenger cars, commercial vehicles, and industrial technology.
The company focuses on driveline and chassis technology, as well as active and passive safety systems for the automotive industry.
ZF's product range targets vehicle manufacturers, mobility providers, and startups in transportation and mobility.
ZF Friedrichshafen AG reported €41.4 billion sales in 2024, down from €46.6 billion in 2023.
The 2024 revenue decline was mainly due to deconsolidation of the axle assembly product line (€2.6 billion sales).
Adjusted EBIT margin was 3.6% in 2024, improved to 4.4% in first half of 2025 and 3.7% in first nine months of 2025.
The company announced workforce reductions of 11,000 to 14,000 employees in Germany by 2028.
In 2025, ZF posted a net loss of €2.1 billion, including a €1.6 billion write-down on electric mobility projects.
ZF is accelerating restructuring efforts and implementing competitiveness programs.

ZF Friedrichshafen AG is a global technology company specializing in advanced mobility products and systems for passenger cars, commercial vehicles, and industrial technology.
The company manufactures driveline and chassis technology, active and passive safety systems, and integrated vehicle systems.

ZF also offers a comprehensive range of aftermarket spare parts through its ZF Aftermarket division, including chassis components under the Lemförder brand such as control arms, stabilizer links, and wheel joints.
Aftermarket parts are available for a wide range of vehicle models, including electric vehicles.
ZF distributes specialized spare parts like switchable engine mounts and dual-mass flywheels designed for ride comfort and reliability.
The company’s product portfolio is primarily aimed at vehicle manufacturers, mobility providers, and startups in transportation and mobility.
ZF Friedrichshafen AG acquired 100% shares of ZF Sachs Micro Mobility GmbH on October 1, 2020.
In December 2025, ZF sold its Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS) business to Harman International.
The axle assembly product line was deconsolidated in 2024, causing a €2.6 billion sales impact and an 11% nominal revenue decline.
ZF placed 8.9 million shares in Haldex AB with institutional investors in September 2019.
The Rubber & Plastics Business Unit was sold to TMT (date not specified).
ZF adopted IAS 8 amendments effective January 1, 2023, with no changes to accounting practices.
In October 2025, ZF agreed to restructure its Electrified Powertrain Technology Division (Division E), including 7,600 job cuts by 2030.
ZF Friedrichshafen AG reported sales of €41.4 billion in 2024, down 11% from €46.6 billion in 2023.
The adjusted EBIT margin decreased from 5.1% in 2023 to 3.6% in 2024.
The sales decline included a €2.6 billion reduction due to the deconsolidation of the axle assembly product line and an organic sales decrease of approximately 3%.
ZF is focusing on strategic realignment, partnerships, and efficiency improvements.
The company is investing in high-margin and forward-looking areas such as software-defined vehicles, automated driving, and e-mobility.
ZF is a world market leader in car chassis technology, leveraging modular chassis 2.0 approaches combining smart actuators and software know-how.
Semiconductor shortages have caused production slowdowns in the German automotive industry, impacting companies including ZF.

Key direct peers include Robert Bosch GmbH, Denso Corporation, Magna International, and CATL, all of which have significant overlaps in driveline, chassis, safety systems, and advanced mobility products. peer_competitors.assessment: ZF Friedrichshafen AG operates in a highly competitive global automotive supplier market dominated by a few large Tier 1 suppliers. Key direct peers include Robert Bosch GmbH, Denso Corporation, Magna International, and CATL, all of which have significant overlaps in driveline, chassis, safety systems, and advanced mobility products. Bosch and ZF, both German companies, compete strongly in Europe and globally, while Denso and Magna provide strong competition from Japan and Canada respectively. CATL, a Chinese company, adds competitive pressure particularly in electric vehicle components and battery technology. The competitive landscape is characterized by a concentration of large multinational suppliers with broad product portfolios serving global OEMs. ZF is positioned as a top five global supplier with a strong presence in driveline and chassis technology, safety systems, and integrated vehicle solutions, maintaining competitiveness through technological innovation and global reach.

companies.name: Fiat Chrysler Automobiles (FCA)
companies.relevance: OEM customer purchasing ZF's 8-speed automatic transmissions for rear-wheel and all-wheel drive vehicles.

companies.name: North American Vehicle Manufacturers
companies.relevance: Major customers for ZF's PowerLine commercial vehicle transmissions, indicating strong OEM demand.

companies.name: ZF Aftermarket Workshop Partners
companies.relevance: Over 15,000 authorized service and repair workshops worldwide supporting ZF products throughout vehicle lifecycles.

companies.name: Mobility Providers and Start-up Companies
companies.relevance: Emerging customers in transportation and mobility sectors utilizing ZF's advanced mobility products and systems.

downstream_buyers.assessment: ZF Friedrichshafen AG's downstream buyer landscape is diverse and global, primarily comprising vehicle OEMs such as Fiat Chrysler Automobiles and other North American manufacturers who integrate ZF's driveline and transmission systems into their vehicles. Additionally, ZF supports a vast aftermarket network with over 15,000 authorized workshop partners worldwide, enabling maintenance, repair, and service of its products throughout their lifecycle. The company also targets mobility providers and start-ups in transportation sectors, reflecting a strategic focus on emerging mobility solutions. This broad buyer base supports multiple monetization and redeployment pathways including OEM supply, aftermarket services, and partnerships with new mobility ventures.

Adaptation of driveline and chassis technology for industrial and commercial vehicle applications
Integration of advanced mobility products into new transportation and mobility platforms

facts: ZF Friedrichshafen AG is a global technology company specializing in advanced mobility products and systems for passenger cars, commercial vehicles, and industrial technology.

ZF also offers a comprehensive range of aftermarket spare parts through its ZF Aftermarket division, including chassis components under the Lemförder brand such as control arms, stabilizer links, and wheel joints.
Aftermarket parts are available for a wide range of vehicle models, including electric vehicles.
ZF distributes specialized spare parts like switchable engine mounts and dual-mass flywheels designed for ride comfort and reliability.
The company’s product portfolio is primarily aimed at vehicle manufacturers, mobility providers, and startups in transportation and mobility.

The presence of specialized aftermarket parts for electric vehicles suggests adaptation to emerging market trends in electrification.

Aftermarket distributors and repair shops may source chassis components and specialized spare parts from ZF’s aftermarket division.
Fleet operators and electric vehicle service providers may be interested in ZF’s aftermarket parts tailored for electric vehicles.

These factors indicate moderate financial pressure but ongoing efforts to improve efficiency and competitiveness.

transaction_event_intelligence.assessment: ZF Friedrichshafen AG has actively managed its portfolio through acquisitions and divestitures to focus on core competencies and improve financial position. Key strategic moves include the acquisition of ZF Sachs Micro Mobility GmbH in 2020 to strengthen micro-mobility capabilities, and the divestiture of its ADAS business to Harman in late 2025 to reduce liabilities. The 2024 deconsolidation of the axle assembly product line significantly impacted revenue. Workforce reductions and restructuring programs, including a major restructuring in Division E announced in 2025 with 7,600 job cuts planned by 2030, indicate ongoing efforts to improve competitiveness amid market challenges. These events collectively suggest moderate financial pressure but strategic realignment to enhance efficiency and focus.

Restructuring efforts accelerated in 2025 to improve competitiveness and reduce costs by over €500 million by 2027.

CompanyDepartment.summary:
ZF Friedrichshafen AG is a global technology company headquartered in Friedrichshafen, Germany, specializing in advanced mobility products, vehicle systems, and industrial technology. The company manufactures driveline and chassis technology, active and passive safety systems, and offers a broad aftermarket spare parts portfolio. ZF is primarily a manufacturer but also distributes and holds stock of spare parts, especially through its ZF Aftermarket division. 

Economically, ZF has faced significant pressure: 2024 revenue fell to €41.4 billion (from €46.6 billion in 2023), mainly due to the deconsolidation of its axle assembly product line. The company posted a net loss of €2.1 billion in 2025, including a €1.6 billion write-down on electric mobility projects, and announced workforce reductions of up to 14,000 employees in Germany by 2028. These signals indicate restructuring and margin pressure, but no explicit inventory stress signals were found.

Financial deep dive results are degraded: while headline revenue, EBIT margin, and major write-downs are confirmed, there is a persistent lack of primary-source inventory, net debt, and working capital figures due to insufficient public data. This is a notable evidence gap.

Product and asset scope is well-supported: ZF manufactures and distributes a wide range of mobility and vehicle system products, with significant aftermarket holdings. The company’s product scope includes both made and distributed goods, with commercially movable inventory in spare parts and components.

Strategic transaction intelligence is strong: recent events include the sale of the ADAS business to Harman International (2025), deconsolidation of the axle assembly line (2024), and divestitures such as the Rubber & Plastics Business Unit. These moves have materially impacted ZF’s revenue, product scope, and potentially its inventory profile.

In summary, confidence is high in ZF’s classification as a manufacturer and distributor with significant aftermarket stock, and in the identification of major economic and strategic events. The main unresolved gap is the absence of detailed, primary-source inventory and balance-sheet data, despite multiple research attempts.

Profitability showed resilience with adjusted EBIT margins improving from 3.6% in 2024 to 4.4% in H1 2025 despite market challenges. The company is actively restructuring, including a significant workforce reduction planned in Germany and strategic write-downs on unprofitable electric mobility projects, resulting in a net loss in 2025. These factors indicate moderate financial pressure but ongoing efforts to improve efficiency and competitiveness.

transaction_event_intelligence.assessment: ZF Friedrichshafen AG has actively managed its portfolio through acquisitions and divestitures to focus on core competencies and improve financial position. Key strategic moves include the acquisition of ZF Sachs Micro Mobility GmbH in 2020 to strengthen micro-mobility capabilities, and the divestiture of its ADAS business to Harman in late 2025 to reduce liabilities. The 2024 deconsolidation of the axle assembly product line significantly impacted revenue. Workforce reductions and restructuring programs, including a major restructuring in Division E announced in 2025 with 7,600 job cuts planned by 2030, indicate ongoing efforts to improve competitiveness amid market challenges. Adoption of IAS 8 amendments shows compliance with accounting standards without changes to practices. These events collectively suggest moderate financial pressure but strategic realignment to enhance efficiency and focus.

MarketDepartment.summary:
Market situation: ZF Friedrichshafen AG operates in the automotive sector, with 2024 sales of €41.4 billion (down 11% YoY), reflecting both divestitures and organic decline. The company faces margin pressure (EBIT margin down to 3.6%) and is responding with strategic realignment and investments in e-mobility, automated driving, and software-defined vehicles. Demand outlook is cautious, with ongoing supply chain challenges (notably semiconductors). However, key market metrics—overall market size, trend direction, and growth rate—could not be substantiated from available evidence and remain open.

Repurposing and circularity: ZF’s reporting confirms product line divestitures and a focus on advanced mobility and industrial technology. However, explicit evidence of circular economy initiatives (reuse, refurbishment, materials recovery) is limited. No clear programs or targets for recycling or remanufacturing were identified, and ZF’s approach to end-of-life management for vehicle systems remains unclear. This is a notable evidence gap for circularity assessment.

Analytics and operational improvement: ZF is affected by industry-wide supply chain disruptions, especially semiconductor shortages, impacting planning and inventory. While the company is pursuing efficiency and realignment, there is no detailed public evidence on specific analytics systems, inventory visibility, or forecasting tools in use. Operational bottlenecks are acknowledged, but the extent of analytics-driven mitigation is not documented. 

Overall, confidence is high in the core findings regarding ZF’s market pressures and strategic direction, but significant gaps remain in quantitative market sizing, circularity initiatives, and analytics detail. These should be flagged for further investigation or direct inquiry with the company.

Strategic investments in emerging technologies signal anticipation of future growth opportunities.
Industry-wide semiconductor shortages represent a supply pressure affecting production capacity.
Deconsolidation of product lines may enable redeployment or repurposing of assets, supporting circular economy practices.

The BuyerDepartment has completed both mandatory tasks for ZF Friedrichshafen AG under the 'peers_buyers_redeployment_aftermarket' classification frame. 

1. Peer Companies: ZF Friedrichshafen AG is confirmed as a leading global Tier 1 automotive supplier, with principal competitors including Robert Bosch GmbH, Denso Corporation, Magna International, and CATL. ZF specializes in driveline and chassis technology, safety systems, and integrated vehicle solutions. The research mapped the competitive landscape and identified key peer companies, but supporting source documentation was lacking, resulting in weak evidence strength. All core classification requirements were met, but the absence of source citations is a notable gap.

2. Monetization and Redeployment Landscape: ZF's primary downstream buyers are major vehicle manufacturers (OEMs), mobility providers, and start-ups. The company operates a global aftermarket division with a large network of authorized workshop partners and targets emerging mobility sectors. The research identified key monetization and redeployment paths, including aftermarket servicing and partnerships with new mobility entrants. However, as with the peer mapping, no supporting sources were recorded, so evidence strength is weak despite all core requirements being satisfied.

In summary, both tasks are complete with all core requirements met, but the lack of supporting source documentation limits confidence in the findings. No tasks were skipped or left unresolved, but evidence gaps should be addressed in future research cycles for higher confidence.

companies.relevance: Denso is a major automotive components manufacturer providing electronic systems and vehicle components, competing with ZF in advanced mobility products and vehicle systems.

peer_competitors.assessment: ZF Friedrichshafen AG operates in a highly competitive global automotive supplier market dominated by a few large Tier 1 suppliers. Key direct peers include Robert Bosch GmbH, Denso Corporation, Magna International, and CATL, all of which have significant overlaps in driveline, chassis, safety systems, and advanced mobility products. Bosch and ZF, both German companies, compete strongly in Europe and globally, while Denso and Magna provide strong competition from Japan and Canada respectively. CATL, a Chinese company, adds competitive pressure particularly in electric vehicle components and battery technology. The competitive landscape is characterized by a concentration of large multinational suppliers with broad product portfolios serving global OEMs. ZF is positioned as a top five global supplier with a strong presence in driveline and chassis technology, safety systems, and integrated vehicle solutions, maintaining competitiveness through technological innovation and global reach.

companies.name: Fiat Chrysler Automobiles (FCA)
companies.relevance: OEM customer purchasing ZF's 8-speed automatic transmissions for rear-wheel and all-wheel drive vehicles.

companies.name: North American Vehicle Manufacturers
companies.relevance: Major customers for ZF's PowerLine commercial vehicle transmissions, indicating strong OEM demand.

companies.name: ZF Aftermarket Workshop Partners
companies.relevance: Over 15,000 authorized service and repair workshops worldwide supporting ZF products throughout vehicle lifecycles.

companies.name: Mobility Providers and Start-up Companies
companies.relevance: Emerging customers in transportation and mobility sectors utilizing ZF's advanced mobility products and systems.

downstream_buyers.assessment: ZF Friedrichshafen AG's downstream buyer landscape is diverse and global, primarily comprising vehicle OEMs such as Fiat Chrysler Automobiles and other North American manufacturers who integrate ZF's driveline and transmission systems into their vehicles. Additionally, ZF supports a vast aftermarket network with over 15,000 authorized workshop partners worldwide, enabling maintenance, repair, and service of its products throughout their lifecycle. The company also targets mobility providers and start-ups in transportation sectors, reflecting a strategic focus on emerging mobility solutions. This broad buyer base supports multiple monetization and redeployment pathways including OEM supply, aftermarket services, and partnerships with new mobility ventures.

ContactDepartment.summary:
The ContactDepartment has completed both mandatory tasks for ZF Friedrichshafen AG. 

1. For prioritized buyer firms (contact_discovery), we identified several relevant decision-makers, including Carl Smiley (Chief Purchasing & Supply Chain Officer, FCA), Antonio Filosa (COO, FCA Latin America), and ZF Group executives such as Dominic Roth (Head of Passenger Car Service and Network Management, ZF Aftermarket), Marc Pregler (Global Commodity Director, MRO Purchasing), and Philippe Colpron (EVP, Head of Aftermarket Division). However, the review flagged a gap: the overall coverage quality was not fully assessed, and there may be additional procurement or operations leaders at other buyer firms or within ZF Aftermarket's partner network that remain unidentified. This is a supporting gap and does not undermine the core findings, which are strong and actionable.

2. For ZF Friedrichshafen AG itself (target_company_contacts), we identified the full Board of Management, including Mathias Miedreich (CEO, responsible for procurement, operations, strategy, transformation, sales, and quality), Michael Frick (CFO), Andreas Moser (Board Member, Commercial Vehicle Solutions, Industrial Technology), and Dr. Lea Corzilius (CHRO, Head of Aftermarket). This task passed all core and supporting criteria, providing high confidence in the completeness and relevance of the contact list for the target company.

In summary, we have high confidence in the identified decision-makers at ZF Friedrichshafen AG and strong, though not exhaustive, coverage of key buyer firm contacts. The main open area is the breadth of procurement/operations contacts at buyer firms beyond those named. No tasks were skipped; all mandatory items are addressed with evidence and documented gaps.

SynthesisDepartment.executive_summary: ZF Friedrichshafen AG is a global Tier 1 automotive supplier under significant economic and operational pressure, with 2024 revenue down 11% to €41.4B, a net loss of €2.1B, and major divestitures and workforce reductions underway. The company’s broad aftermarket and global buyer network create multiple entry points for Liquisto, especially in excess inventory disposition and asset redeployment. While ZF’s restructuring and margin compression signal strong potential for surplus asset solutions, there are persistent evidence gaps in inventory, working capital, and circularity initiatives. Outreach should prioritize ZF’s Board and Aftermarket leadership, positioning Liquisto’s services as direct responses to ZF’s current challenges, and use buyer/peer intelligence to tailor the approach. Direct engagement is recommended to clarify open questions and refine the opportunity.

SynthesisDepartment.buyer_market_summary: ZF Friedrichshafen AG's downstream buyer landscape is diverse and global, primarily comprising vehicle OEMs such as Fiat Chrysler Automobiles and other North American manufacturers who integrate ZF's driveline and transmission systems into their vehicles. Additionally, ZF supports a vast aftermarket network with over 15,000 authorized workshop partners worldwide, enabling maintenance, repair, and service of its products throughout their lifecycle. The company also targets mobility providers and start-ups in transportation sectors, reflecting a strategic focus on emerging mobility solutions. This broad buyer base supports multiple monetization and redeployment pathways including OEM supply, aftermarket services, and partnerships with new mobility ventures.

facts: ZF Friedrichshafen AG is a global technology company specializing in advanced mobility products and systems for passenger cars, commercial vehicles, and industrial technology.
The company manufactures driveline and chassis technology, active and passive safety systems, and integrated vehicle systems.

ZF also offers a comprehensive range of aftermarket spare parts through its ZF Aftermarket division, including chassis components under the Lemförder brand such as control arms, stabilizer links, and wheel joints.
Aftermarket parts are available for a wide range of vehicle models, including electric vehicles.
ZF distributes specialized spare parts like switchable engine mounts and dual-mass flywheels designed for ride comfort and reliability.
The company’s product portfolio is primarily aimed at vehicle manufacturers, mobility providers, and startups in transportation and mobility.
market_signals: ZF’s product portfolio includes both manufactured core vehicle systems and distributed aftermarket spare parts, indicating a dual role as manufacturer and distributor.
The presence of specialized aftermarket parts for electric vehicles suggests adaptation to emerging market trends in electrification.
The company’s restructuring and deconsolidation of some product lines may impact the scope of products held or distributed in inventory.
buyer_hypotheses: Vehicle manufacturers and mobility providers likely purchase driveline, chassis, and safety systems directly from ZF as manufactured products.
Aftermarket distributors and repair shops may source chassis components and specialized spare parts from ZF’s aftermarket division.
Fleet operators and electric vehicle service providers may be interested in ZF’s aftermarket parts tailored for electric vehicles.

These factors indicate moderate financial pressure but ongoing efforts to improve efficiency and competitiveness.

facts: ZF Friedrichshafen AG was founded in 1915 by Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin and Alfred von Soden-Fraunhofen.
The company is headquartered in Friedrichshafen, Baden-Württemberg, Germany.
As of 2025, ZF Friedrichshafen AG employs approximately 153,000 people.
ZF is a global technology company supplying advanced mobility products and systems for passenger cars, commercial vehicles, and industrial technology.
The company focuses on driveline and chassis technology, as well as active and passive safety systems for the automotive industry.
ZF's product range targets vehicle manufacturers, mobility providers, and startups in transportation and mobility.
ZF Friedrichshafen AG reported €41.4 billion sales in 2024, down from €46.6 billion in 2023.
The 2024 revenue decline was mainly due to deconsolidation of the axle assembly product line (€2.6 billion sales).
Adjusted EBIT margin was 3.6% in 2024, improved to 4.4% in first half of 2025 and 3.7% in first nine months of 2025.
The company announced workforce reductions of 11,000 to 14,000 employees in Germany by 2028.
In 2025, ZF posted a net loss of €2.1 billion, including a €1.6 billion write-down on electric mobility projects.
ZF is accelerating restructuring efforts and implementing competitiveness programs.
ZF Friedrichshafen AG reported €41.4 billion revenue in 2024, down 11% nominally from €46.6 billion in 2023, mainly due to deconsolidation of axle assembly product line (€2.6 billion sales impact).
Adjusted EBIT margin was 3.6% in 2024, improving to 4.4% in H1 2025 and 3.7% in first 9 months of 2025.
In 2025, ZF recorded a net loss of €2.1 billion, including a €1.6 billion write-down on electric mobility projects.
The company announced workforce reductions of 11,000 to 14,000 employees in Germany by 2028 as part of restructuring.
No explicit inventory or net debt figures were found in the provided excerpts; these are expected in the detailed 2024 Annual Report PDF.
ZF Friedrichshafen AG is a global technology company specializing in advanced mobility products and systems for passenger cars, commercial vehicles, and industrial technology.
The company manufactures driveline and chassis technology, active and passive safety systems, and integrated vehicle systems.

ZF also offers a comprehensive range of aftermarket spare parts through its ZF Aftermarket division, including chassis components under the Lemförder brand such as control arms, stabilizer links, and wheel joints.
Aftermarket parts are available for a wide range of vehicle models, including electric vehicles.
ZF distributes specialized spare parts like switchable engine mounts and dual-mass flywheels designed for ride comfort and reliability.
The company’s product portfolio is primarily aimed at vehicle manufacturers, mobility providers, and startups in transportation and mobility.
ZF Friedrichshafen AG acquired 100% shares of ZF Sachs Micro Mobility GmbH on October 1, 2020.
In December 2025, ZF sold its Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS) business to Harman International.
The axle assembly product line was deconsolidated in 2024, causing a €2.6 billion sales impact and an 11% nominal revenue decline.
ZF placed 8.9 million shares in Haldex AB with institutional investors in September 2019.
The Rubber & Plastics Business Unit was sold to TMT (date not specified).
ZF adopted IAS 8 amendments effective January 1, 2023, with no changes to accounting practices.
In October 2025, ZF agreed to restructure its Electrified Powertrain Technology Division (Division E), including 7,600 job cuts by 2030.

facts: ZF Friedrichshafen AG is a global technology company specializing in advanced mobility products and systems for passenger cars, commercial vehicles, and industrial technology.
The company manufactures driveline and chassis technology, active and passive safety systems, and integrated vehicle systems.

ZF also offers a comprehensive range of aftermarket spare parts through its ZF Aftermarket division, including chassis components under the Lemförder brand such as control arms, stabilizer links, and wheel joints.
Aftermarket parts are available for a wide range of vehicle models, including electric vehicles.
ZF distributes specialized spare parts like switchable engine mounts and dual-mass flywheels designed for ride comfort and reliability.
The company’s product portfolio is primarily aimed at vehicle manufacturers, mobility providers, and startups in transportation and mobility.

recent_events: 2024 deconsolidation of axle assembly product line (€2.6 billion sales impact)

economic_situation.assessment: ZF Friedrichshafen AG experienced a nominal revenue decline of 11% in 2024 primarily due to the deconsolidation of a major product line, with an organic decline of about 3%. Profitability showed resilience with adjusted EBIT margins improving from 3.6% in 2024 to 4.4% in H1 2025 despite market challenges. The company is actively restructuring, including a significant workforce reduction planned in Germany and strategic write-downs on unprofitable electric mobility projects, resulting in a net loss in 2025. These factors indicate moderate financial pressure but ongoing efforts to improve efficiency and competitiveness.

financial_deep_dive.assessment: ZF Friedrichshafen AG faced moderate financial pressure in 2024-2025, with nominal revenue decline driven by deconsolidation and organic contraction. Profitability showed resilience with improving adjusted EBIT margins despite market challenges. The company is actively restructuring, including workforce reductions and strategic write-downs on electric mobility projects, resulting in a net loss in 2025. Inventory write-downs and restructuring efforts suggest cautious balance sheet management amid transformation.

facts: ZF Friedrichshafen AG acquired 100% shares of ZF Sachs Micro Mobility GmbH on October 1, 2020.
In December 2025, ZF sold its Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS) business to Harman International.
The axle assembly product line was deconsolidated in 2024, causing a €2.6 billion sales impact and an 11% nominal revenue decline.
ZF placed 8.9 million shares in Haldex AB with institutional investors in September 2019.
The Rubber & Plastics Business Unit was sold to TMT (date not specified).
ZF adopted IAS 8 amendments effective January 1, 2023, with no changes to accounting practices.
In October 2025, ZF agreed to restructure its Electrified Powertrain Technology Division (Division E), including 7,600 job cuts by 2030.

2025 accelerated restructuring efforts with improved competitiveness programs
2025 net loss of €2.1 billion including €1.6 billion write-down on electric mobility projects
economic_situation.assessment: ZF Friedrichshafen AG experienced a nominal revenue decline of 11% in 2024 primarily due to the deconsolidation of a major product line, with an organic decline of about 3%. Profitability showed resilience with adjusted EBIT margins improving from 3.6% in 2024 to 4.4% in H1 2025 despite market challenges. The company is actively restructuring, including a significant workforce reduction planned in Germany and strategic write-downs on unprofitable electric mobility projects, resulting in a net loss in 2025. These factors indicate moderate financial pressure but ongoing efforts to improve efficiency and competitiveness.

financial_deep_dive.assessment: ZF Friedrichshafen AG faced moderate financial pressure in 2024-2025, with nominal revenue decline driven by deconsolidation and organic contraction. Profitability showed resilience with improving adjusted EBIT margins despite market challenges. The company is actively restructuring, including workforce reductions and strategic write-downs on electric mobility projects, resulting in a net loss in 2025. Inventory write-downs and restructuring efforts suggest cautious balance sheet management amid transformation.

peer_competitors.assessment: ZF Friedrichshafen AG operates in a highly competitive global automotive supplier market dominated by a few large Tier 1 suppliers. Key direct peers include Robert Bosch GmbH, Denso Corporation, Magna International, and CATL, all of which have significant overlaps in driveline, chassis, safety systems, and advanced mobility products. Bosch and ZF, both German companies, compete strongly in Europe and globally, while Denso and Magna provide strong competition from Japan and Canada respectively. CATL, a Chinese company, adds competitive pressure particularly in electric vehicle components and battery technology. The competitive landscape is characterized by a concentration of large multinational suppliers with broad product portfolios serving global OEMs. ZF is positioned as a top five global supplier with a strong presence in driveline and chassis technology, safety systems, and integrated vehicle solutions, maintaining competitiveness through technological innovation and global reach.

facts: ZF Friedrichshafen AG's Board of Management consists of five members as of 2026.
Mathias Miedreich is CEO responsible for procurement, operations, strategy, transformation, sales, and quality.
Michael Frick is CFO responsible for finance, M&A, IT/digital, and passive safety systems.
Andreas Moser is Board Member responsible for Commercial Vehicle Solutions, Industrial Technology, and India Region.
Dr. Lea Corzilius is CHRO and Head of Aftermarket division.
Dominic Roth is Head of Passenger Car Service and Network Management at ZF Aftermarket.
The company is actively restructuring with focus on cautious balance sheet management and inventory write-downs.

These leaders are key stakeholders for inventory-to-cash and working capital optimization discussions.

ZF Friedrichshafen AG's strategic realignment, including deconsolidation of product lines, indicates a focus on optimizing asset utilization and enhancing circularity through repurposing components. Analytics could add value by improving supply chain planning, inventory visibility, and decision support to mitigate supply pressures and support operational efficiency.. Demand outlook: ZF Friedrichshafen AG reported sales of €41.4 billion in 2024, down 11% from €46.6 billion in 2023. The adjusted EBIT margin decreased from 5.1% in 2023 to 3.6% in 2024..
